title: istio-cni: failed to remove pod from mesh
body:
### Is this the right place to submit this?

- [X] This is not a security vulnerability or a crashing bug
- [X] This is not a question about how to use Istio

### Bug Description

**Namespaces previously added to ambient mesh are not deleted**

After removing the label (**istio.io/dataplane-mode**) from the **tools** namespace:

`kubectl label ns tools istio.io/dataplane-mode-`

the **tools** namespace continues to be in the ambient mesh:

`./istioctl ztunnel-config workload`

![2024-11-08 09 56 26](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02ccf617-bfd0-409e-aaf1-a7043a040ff7)

istio-cni logs:
![2024-11-08 10 09 58](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae159d17-42d3-4b3a-9a4c-c0e8c7531303)



### Version

```Text
control plane version: 1.24.0
k8s: v1.30.4
CNI Plugin: cilium v1.16.3
```


### Additional Information

_No response_

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> allow non-apparmor users to opt out

My only concern with this is the same one I had before - making it a user-facing knob is easy to misunderstand/abuse if we aren't careful - I want to avoid people getting in to the trap of thinking "I can make `istio-cni` unprivileged if I set `privileged=false`" - which they _can never_ do. It is _always_ a privileged pod, in reality and as per the Kubernetes PSS.

If we let people opt-out, I'm very much not clear how we would message that in a way that wouldn't confuse the hell out of 99% of the people looking at that flag.

Maybe exposing it as `values.appArmorBypass=true|false` would be enough. If you don't have appArmor you can set it to `false`.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: I agree that making privileged a user facing nob would reintroduce the confusion we were trying to avoid. A `values.appArmorBypass` flag makes sense to me. However, how many users would install istio not knowing apparmor is enabled and spend extra cycles debugging?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> I agree that making privileged a user facing nob would reintroduce the confusion we were trying to avoid. A `values.appArmorBypass` flag makes sense to me. However, how many users would install istio not knowing apparmor is enabled and spend extra cycles debugging?

Yeah - I think we would have to default `appArmorBypass` to `true` (to echo what @participant1 said above)

If you _know_ you aren't using appArmor, you can opt-in to setting it to false.


...if we are 100% sure that `appArmor: unconfined` doesn't work, as that would be preferable.

The pods still fail to be removed from the mesh because of failures related to deleting nonexistent raw iptable rules. 

- https://github.com/istio/istio/pull/53888 Should resolve the AppArmor failures.
- https://github.com/istio/istio/pull/53153 Should resolve the iptable failures.

```bash
# create namespace and add it to mesh
kubectl create ns nethost
kubectl label namespace auth istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient --overwrite
# run iptables-save/ss -tpln in one terminal 
kubectl run --rm -it nethost --image=nicolaka/netshoot --restart=Never --privileged -n nethost -- watch -n1 'iptables-save; ss -tpln'
```

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
@participant6 I suspect that the error you have in the logs about inpod rules not being deleted correctly should be addressed by my commit, that error led to an early exit in the RemovePodFromMesh() when certain iptables cfgs are used.

I noticed the same problem while working on the test cases for the idempotency/reconciliation PR so I tried to fix it.
From the description of my PR:
> - Resolved in-pod deletion errors caused by the deletion logic incorrectly assuming that certain commands would work, even when the relevant rules were not present. The creation of these rules depends on the values of tproxy and ingressMode. Therefore, certain failed deletion commands cannot reliably indicate successful deletion. See https://github.com/istio/istio/commit/1b03f56e1476cf850afe11f70abdb15ed810e686.

On the other end, I cannot say for sure why sometimes you experienced the issue and sometimes you did not as I'm not well versed in the cni-agent logic.
